records.source: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאַ֭שְׁרֵי כָּל־יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה הַ֝הֹלֵ֗ךְ בִּדְרָכָֽיו׃
records.gloss: The song of the ascents. How blessed [is] everyone who fears YHWH, who walks in his ways.
pieces: A song of ascents. How blessed is everyone who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and lives the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} directs!

L.1: A song of ascents. How blessed [is] everyone who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who walks in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways!

R.1: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. Life is truly good for everyone who honors {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and lives the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: How blessed: how good the life of
decisions.reason: The exclamation ('ashre) of 1:1. Verse 4 sums up the psalm with a different word: "blessed" (barak), blessed by the LORD.

decisions.choice: fears: reveres
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to take him seriously as God, with awe and obedience (Proverbs 1:7). The next line says what it looks like: walking in his ways.

decisions.choice: walks in his ways: lives as he directs
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a common picture for how a person lives (1:1; Deuteronomy 8:6).

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for; honors
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 33:18.

records.heading: The blessing on those who fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: יְגִ֣יעַ כַּ֭פֶּיךָ כִּ֣י תֹאכֵ֑ל אַ֝שְׁרֶ֗יךָ וְט֣וֹב לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: The toil of your hands, for you will eat; how blessed you [are], and good [will be] to you.
pieces: You will enjoy the food your own hands have worked for; how blessed you will be, and how good your life!

L.2: The toil of your hands — surely you will eat [it]; how blessed you [will be], and [it will be] good for you!

R.2: You will eat what you have worked for. Life will be truly good for you, and all will go well.

decisions.choice: eat the toil of your hands: enjoy what you work for
decisions.reason: To eat the toil of one's hands is to enjoy the harvest of one's own work, not to see it taken by enemies or lost to drought (Deuteronomy 28:33; Isaiah 62:8-9).

decisions.choice: for: surely
decisions.reason: The word (ki) here stresses the promise: "you will surely eat".

decisions.choice: you: the one who fears the LORD
decisions.reason: The psalm turns from describing (verse 1) to speaking directly to the one who fears the LORD.

records.source: אֶשְׁתְּךָ֤׀כְּגֶ֥פֶן פֹּרִיָּה֮ בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֪י בֵ֫יתֶ֥ךָ בָּ֭נֶיךָ כִּשְׁתִלֵ֣י זֵיתִ֑ים סָ֝בִ֗יב לְשֻׁלְחָנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Your wife [will be] like a vine fruitful in [the] innermost parts of your house; your children like shoots of olive trees around your table.
pieces: In the heart of your home your wife will be like a vine loaded with grapes, and around your table your children will be like young olive plants.

L.3: Your wife [will be] like a fruitful vine in the inner parts of your house; your children like shoots of olive trees around your table.

R.3: Your wife will have many children, like a grapevine full of fruit in your home. Your children will gather around your table, healthy and strong like young olive trees.

decisions.choice: vine and olive: pictures of a rich life
decisions.reason: The vine and the olive were the main crops of the land (Deuteronomy 8:8). A fruitful vine pictures a wife who bears children; young olive shoots, from a tree that lives for centuries, picture healthy children and a family that will last (52:10).

decisions.choice: the innermost parts of your house: the heart of the home
decisions.reason: The word (yarkete) means the farthest or innermost part; here the inner rooms of the family home.

decisions.choice: will have many children; healthy and strong
decisions.reason: Readable says what each picture means (m1).

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה כִי־כֵ֭ן יְבֹ֥רַךְ גָּ֗בֶר יְרֵ֣א יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, for so will be blessed a man who fears YHWH.
pieces: See how {{gender:the one|the man}} who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be blessed!

L.4: Look, for so will {{gender:the one|the man}} be blessed who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: This is how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blesses {{gender:anyone|a man}} who honors {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: blessed: given good by the LORD
decisions.reason: This verb (barak) is not the exclamation of verse 1 but the word for a blessing given; verse 5 names the LORD as the one who gives it.

decisions.choice: the one; anyone
decisions.reason: As in 127:5: the word (gever) is "a man", here the husband and father of verse 3; the default makes the blessing general and the gender setting gives "the man".

decisions.choice: the LORD blesses ... who honors him
alternatives: will be blessed ... who fears the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who blesses (verse 5) and says "honor" for fear, as in verse 1.

records.source: יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָ֗ה מִצִּ֫יּ֥וֹן וּ֭רְאֵה בְּט֣וּב יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: May YHWH bless you from Zion, and see the good of Jerusalem all [the] days of your life,
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} send you blessing from Zion, and may you look on Jerusalem's good fortune as long as you live,

L.5: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you from Zion, and see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life,

R.5: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you from Zion. May you see Jerusalem doing well every day of your life.

decisions.choice: from Zion: from the LORD's house
decisions.reason: Blessing comes from Zion because the LORD's house is there (20:3; 134:3).

decisions.choice: and see: may you see
decisions.reason: The command "see" here expresses a wish that goes with the blessing: may you live to see it. The sentence runs on into verse 6.

decisions.choice: the good of Jerusalem: its prosperity
decisions.reason: The good (tuv) of the city is its peace and well-being (122:9).

records.gloss: and see children of your children. Peace [be] on Israel.
pieces: and may you live long enough to see your grandchildren. May Israel have peace!

L.6: and see children of your children. Peace [be] upon Israel.

R.6: May you live long enough to see your grandchildren. May Israel have peace!

decisions.choice: children of your children: a long life
decisions.reason: To see one's grandchildren is a sign of a long, blessed life (Genesis 50:23; Proverbs 17:6).

decisions.choice: peace on Israel: a closing blessing
decisions.reason: As in 125:5, the blessing on one household widens to the whole people.
